entities.name: Bangkok National Museum
entities.label: Institution
entities.summary:
The Bangkok National Museum (พิพิธภัณฑสถานแห่งชาติพระนคร, National Museum Bangkok), established in 1874 by King Chulalongkorn (Rama V) as a public museum — the first in Thailand — and housed in part of the former Wang Na (Front Palace) complex adjacent to the Grand Palace complex, is Thailand's largest and most comprehensive museum, with collections spanning Thai art and history from prehistoric periods through the Bangkok period Rattanakosin era, and one of the finest collections of Southeast Asian art in the world.

The museum's founding by Chulalongkorn was part of his extraordinary modernization program that saved Siam from direct colonization by demonstrating to European powers that Siam was a civilized, modern state. The Wang Na complex (former residence of the Vice-King or 'Second King') was converted to museum use after the Vice-Kingship was abolished. Chulalongkorn's museum initiative, alongside his railroad-building, educational reforms, and abolition of slavery, established Thailand's modern institutional infrastructure.

The museum's collection is extraordinary: prehistoric artifacts from the Ban Chiang culture (among the world's earliest bronze-using cultures, ca. 2100 BC), Dvaravati Buddhist art (6th-11th centuries), Khmer-period art from when much of modern Thailand was under Khmer Empire influence, Sukhothai and Ayutthaya-period masterworks, and the finest collection of royal regalia, thrones, carriages, and ceremonial objects representing Thai royal culture. The museum includes Buddhaisawan Chapel (1795) housing one of Thailand's most sacred Buddha images, the Phra Phuttha Sihing.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: Bangkok National Museum — Thailand's oldest and largest museum, founded by Chulalongkorn as evidence of Thai civilization while resisting colonization, housing Ban Chiang prehistoric bronzes and the sacred Phra Phuttha Sihing, and containing one of the world's finest Southeast Asian art collections — is Central Thailand's most important cultural institution.
